newsitem.title: UK: U.K. Intervention Board details EU sugar sales.
newsitem.headline: U.K. Intervention Board details EU sugar sales.

text.p: A total 34,750 tonnes of current series white sugar received export rebates of a maximum 43.835 European Currency Units (Ecus) per 100 kilos at Wednesday's European Union (EU) tender, the U.K. Intervention Board said.
Traders in France received all the tonnage, it added.

This week's award brings the cumulative tonnage awarded for export from the 1996/97 crop to 1.598 million tonnes. This compares with the 2,000 tonnes awarded on March 6, 1996, when the cumulative tonnage totalled 1.603 million tonnes.
Earlier on Wednesday, London traders had expected the subsidy for the current season whites campaign for licences to end-August to be 43.835 Ecus, the exact amount awarded.
Traders had also forecast the total authorised sugar tonnage export awards to be between 40,000 and 70,000 tonnes versus 30,300 last week when the restitution was 44.471 Ecus.
